A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Cropper. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and supplementary material are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial experimental and presentation changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original cropping benchmarks, retrieval/refinement ablations, a user study and color-enhancement demonstrations.

after.justification: v2 reports original cropping benchmarks, scorer and VLM ablations, output-selection experiments and a redesigned user study.

M1.justification: v2 extends VILA-only aesthetic feedback with crop-area and CLIP content-preservation scoring, using task-specific combinations. Aspect-ratio cropping changes from predicting (x,y,w) with calculated height to predicting four box coordinates with ratio instructions. The color-enhancement adaptation is removed.

E1.justification: GAICD and FCDB free-form cropping and SACD subject-aware cropping remain. However, GNMC aspect-ratio evaluation is replaced by aspect-ratio evaluation on FCDB, and the MIT-Adobe FiveK color-enhancement task disappears entirely, including its supplementary examples.

E2.justification: The supervised comparator sets for GAICD, FCDB free-form cropping and SACD are retained. The aspect-ratio comparison drops GNMC and introduces Mars, A2RL and VPN. Qualitative VLM comparisons change to GPT-4o and Gemini 1.5 Pro; VPN disappears from the user study and CGS from the free-form visual comparison. Color-enhancement comparisons are removed.

E3.justification: Free-form defaults change from Gemini-pro-vision with 10 examples, 5 candidates and 10 iterations to Gemini 1.5 Pro with 30 examples, 6 candidates and 2 iterations. Parameter selection moves from GAICD test data to validation data. The user study changes from five-way choices on 100 images with ten raters to pairwise comparisons on 200 test images with five raters.

E4.justification: v2 adds scorer-combination ablations across all three cropping tasks, final-iteration versus highest-score selection, VLM comparisons and temperature sensitivity (Tables 5, 8, 9, 14, 16 and Figure 5). Parameter-count studies are revised. v1's joint example/candidate-count analysis and before/after aesthetic-score plot are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed statistics, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. Changes to user-study image and rater counts concern evaluation design rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Under revised models/settings, Cropper's GAICD Acc5/Acc10 changes from 83.5/94.0 to 84.3/96.5 (Table 2), while FCDB free-form IoU/Disp changes from 0.752/0.062 to 0.667/0.087 (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 12). Numerous ablation and aspect-ratio results are replaced or added. The user-study results change from 29% five-way preference to 60.8–63.4% pairwise preference; these percentages are not directly comparable.

T1.justification: v2 introduces the normalized crop-area scoring definition A = Hcrop Wcrop / (HW) in Section 4.1. The retrieval maximizations remain essentially unchanged apart from notation and cardinality clarification. Neither version contains theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of training-free, unified cropping through prompt retrieval and iterative refinement remain. v2 narrows the concluding scope by dropping v1's claim of successful applications beyond cropping, following removal of the color-enhancement extension.

C2.justification: v2 adds content-preservation explanations for area and CLIP scoring, task-dependent recommendations for scoring and output selection, and discussion of VLM performance/latency tradeoffs. Its limitations discussion shifts from retrieval-database quality and long-context understanding to inference speed constrained by example retrieval.

D1.justification: v2 replaces illustrated prompt walkthroughs with revised task-specific templates and adds a zero-shot prompt, temperature and backbone-specific settings, latency figures and user-study instructions. Color-editing implementation details disappear. Documentation remains uneven: the free-form ground-truth crop count becomes an unspecified T, and scorer-combination rules are not fully specified.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Mars, Mantis, Gemini 1.5 and Unsplash, while removing references associated with GNMC, FiveK, Distort-and-recover, MTurk and Liu et al.'s GPT-3 example-selection work. The central positioning relative to supervised cropping and visual in-context learning remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: parameter-selection discussion moves into implementation details, ablations receive separate topical discussions, and the FCDB free-form comparison moves to the supplement. The supplement is rewritten into task-based sections and user-study instructions, replacing its earlier prompt-gallery structure. The conclusion is condensed and combined with limitations.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column to a two-column layout. Overview diagrams and most qualitative panels are redesigned, parameter plots are replaced, and new ablation tables are introduced. The user-study pie chart becomes a pairwise-results table, the FCDB table moves to the supplement, and the extensive illustrated prompt galleries disappear.

improvement.justification: Moving reported parameter selection from test data to validation data improves the evaluation design. Targeted scorer, output-selection and VLM ablations make the revised design choices easier to assess, and Appendix D clarifies user-study instructions. These gains support a limited net improvement, tempered by incomplete scorer-combination details and the loss of the earlier long-context limitations discussion.
